Samir —

Thanks for the inventory; looks comprehensive. Quick notes up front, then proposed next steps: 

Top-level guidance:
- Use blockstore (iSCSI/Ceph RBD) for model artifacts (read-heavy, large objects) and local NVMe for KV/prefix cache. Avoid mounting model volumes as ephemeral on preflight — prefer stable blockstore mounts with late bind during node boot.
- Attach protocol: we recommend CSI multi-stage attach with explicit lateBind: true in StorageClass for model volumes. This reduces repeated remount churn during node restarts and speeds scheduling.
- Attach limits: aim for <= 32 concurrent blockstore attaches per node; target 2–3 attach operations per second per rack under normal load. If you anticipate spikes, plan a per-rack attach-throttle gateway (we can provide a small sidecar).

Nodepool proposal (3 racks, 48 nodes total):
- control-plane (3 dedicated control nodes, spread across racks)
- infra (6 nodes — logging/ingress/metrics)
- worker-general (26 nodes)
- worker-gpu (13 nodes) — sized for model concurrency; can burst to worker-general if needed

Next steps:

- Irene to share attach-step sample and known kernel/driver caveats for Dell/Lenovo racks.
- Vanessa to confirm retention/RPO/KMS requirements that affect PV encryption and audit config.

Samir / team —

Following up with the more technical checklist Michael referenced. High level and then a short ops example.

Checklist (things we will validate during preflight):
- Kernel/driver versions (Linux distros): ensure multipath-tools >= 0.8 and iscsi-initiator-utils updated; known issue with Dell iDRAC firmware 4.1 — requires iscsi init workaround (we’ll provide exact commands).
- iSCSI target topology: prefer per-rack gateway with LACP bond to reduce cross-rack attach latency.
- StorageClass settings: allowVolumeExpansion=true, volumeBindingMode=WaitForFirstConsumer for local-cache StorageClass; for models use volumeBindingMode=Immediate but with CSI staged attach disabled until node is ready.
- CSI: implement ControllerPublishVolume with exponential backoff and a 60s attach timeout.
- Pod-level: use node affinity + tolerations for disk-local pods to ensure cache locality.

Ops sample (attach sequence):
1) Pod scheduled -> PVC created -> kubelet waits for ControllerPublishVolume
2) ControllerPublish triggers CSI attach to node via per-rack attach gateway
3) Node receives attach event -> mount namespace prepared -> mount completes -> application starts

Known limits: most mainstream drivers maintain ~32 active attach endpoints per node; if you expect >32 model disks per node, consolidate models into a single large block or use an object-store-backed pattern.

Attachment: small ops snippet with iscsi multipath checks.

I can walk this during the call and run a quick compatibility check on your inventory.

Samir —

Adding the compliance and ops-readout items so nothing surprises go-live: 

- Data residency & encryption: model artifacts on blockstore must be encrypted-at-rest using customer KMS. We’ll need key-wrap policy and an HSM/KMS endpoint reachable from the private control plane.
- Audit & retention: Redwood Private can stream mount/attach audit logs to your SIEM (we recommend 90 days hot, 365 days cold). Confirm if Northstar needs longer RPOs.
- Access controls: recommend role-separated vault access for secrets and a read-only service account for model pulls where possible.
